description: Gold set for calibrating atomic-claim adjudication thresholds (min_entailment_percent, contradiction_threshold_percent). Each case pairs a claim with one evidence snippet and the expected NLI verdict. Human-reviewed for factual accuracy.

cases.claim: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776.
cases.evidence_snippet: Declaration of Independence adoption date: July 4, 1776. Delegates at the Second Continental Congress voted to approve the declaration.

cases.claim: The Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1812.
cases.evidence_snippet: Declaration of Independence adoption date: July 4, 1776.

cases.claim: George Washington was the first president of the United States.
cases.evidence_snippet: George Washington served as the first President of the United States from 1789 to 1797.

cases.claim: George Washington was the third president.
cases.evidence_snippet: George Washington was the first president of the United States, not the third.

cases.claim: The Civil War began in 1861.
cases.evidence_snippet: American Civil War start date: April 12, 1861 (attack on Fort Sumter).

cases.claim: The Civil War ended in 1865.
cases.evidence_snippet: American Civil War end date: April 9, 1865 (Lee's surrender at Appomattox).

cases.claim: The 13th Amendment abolished slavery.
cases.evidence_snippet: Thirteenth Amendment ratified December 6, 1865, formally abolished slavery in the United States.

cases.claim: The Emancipation Proclamation freed all slaves in the United States.
cases.evidence_snippet: The Emancipation Proclamation applied only to Confederate states in rebellion and did not free enslaved people in border states or Union-held territories.

cases.claim: The 19th Amendment gave women the right to vote.
cases.evidence_snippet: Nineteenth Amendment ratified August 18, 1920; granted women the right to vote.

cases.claim: The 19th Amendment was ratified in 1910.
cases.evidence_snippet: Nineteenth Amendment ratification date: August 18, 1920.

cases.claim: The United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in 1945.
cases.evidence_snippet: Atomic bombing of Hiroshima: August 6, 1945; Nagasaki: August 9, 1945.

cases.claim: Pearl Harbor was attacked in 1914.
cases.evidence_snippet: Attack on Pearl Harbor occurred on December 7, 1941.

cases.claim: The Brown v. Board of Education decision declared segregation unconstitutional.
cases.evidence_snippet: Brown v. Board of Education, decided May 17, 1954, ruled racial segregation in public schools unconstitutional.

cases.claim: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 was signed by President Eisenhower.
cases.evidence_snippet: Civil Rights Act of 1964 was signed by President Lyndon B. Johnson on July 2, 1964, not by Eisenhower.

cases.claim: The Apollo 11 mission landed astronauts on the Moon in 1969.
cases.evidence_snippet: Apollo 11 lunar landing: July 20, 1969; Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans on the Moon.

cases.claim: The Louisiana Purchase doubled the size of the United States.
cases.evidence_snippet: Louisiana Purchase completed 1803; United States land area approximately doubled as a result.

cases.claim: The New Deal was a military alliance signed in 1945.
cases.evidence_snippet: The New Deal was a domestic economic recovery program enacted 1933–1939 under Franklin D. Roosevelt, not a military alliance.

cases.claim: The Affordable Care Act was signed in 2010.
cases.evidence_snippet: Affordable Care Act signed March 23, 2010 by President Barack Obama.

cases.claim: Abraham Lincoln was the 16th President of the United States.
cases.evidence_snippet: Abraham Lincoln was the 16th President, serving from 1861 to 1865.

cases.claim: Abraham Lincoln was the 20th President of the United States.
cases.evidence_snippet: Abraham Lincoln was the 16th President of the United States, not the 20th.

cases.claim: The Great Depression began in 1929.
cases.evidence_snippet: The Great Depression began with the stock market crash of October 1929.

cases.claim: The United States entered World War I in 1920.
cases.evidence_snippet: The United States declared war on Germany and entered World War I on April 6, 1917, not in 1920.

cases.claim: The Constitutional Convention met in Philadelphia in 1787.
cases.evidence_snippet: The Constitutional Convention convened in Philadelphia in 1787 to draft a new constitution.

cases.claim: The Voting Rights Act was signed in 1965.
cases.evidence_snippet: Voting Rights Act of 1965 signed August 6, 1965, prohibiting discriminatory voting practices.
